surfaces.part: green sign panel with white lettering

answer.evidence: The main body is a tall flat sign panel drawn face-on (rows 8-29), with a green field, white text and a dark outline. Its width is a constant 14 px from rows 1-30, so there is no ellipse or widening and narrowing. The gray header at rows 1-6 has a highlight at the top and a darker row 6 above the dark outline at row 7. It reads as a front-facing box, with no front-edge line or eave shadow, so no horizontal top surface is shown. No side face or roof plane is drawn. This matches the front-elevation reference (flat face, no top).

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical sign panel with a dark green-teal rim, a lighter inner bevel and highlight edge, a mid-green face and white glyphs, so about 5 lightness steps. That matches the kiosk and vending references and is above the bus shelter, which has about 4-5 steps. The measured facts back this up: 12 visible tones per tile equals kiosk-a (12) and is well above bus-shelter-a (6), though below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, against 9% for bus-shelter-a. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans green rather than black, as it does in the references. The glyphs and bevel break up the face, so there is no large flat fill. It is a simple sign and slightly less textured than the vending machine, but a careful artist would accept it next to these references without it looking flatter or more sticker-like.
